issues.failure_explanation: In Theorem 3.4, the proof correctly bounds the root mean square error (\EV{|c_k - \tilde{c}_k^{(m)}|^2})^{1/2} by \sqrt{\lambda_k} \delta_{\gamma, h} C h^{\min(\gamma - 1/2, m+1)} (and by \sqrt{\lambda_k} \mu_k^{-1/q} C h^{m+1} in Part 2). However, in the statement of Theorem 3.4, the author squares the LHS and the power of h to h^{\min(2\gamma-1, 2m+2)}, but fails to square \sqrt{\lambda_k}, \delta_{\gamma, h}, and \mu_k^{-1/q}. Consequently, the stated inequality is inhomogeneous in the noise covariance Q (scaling as \sqrt{\lambda_k} on the RHS versus \lambda_k on the LHS) and is mathematically false for sufficiently large \lambda_k.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace \sqrt{\lambda_k} by \lambda_k, \delta_{\gamma, h} by \delta_{\gamma, h}^2, and \mu_k^{-1/q} by \mu_k^{-2/q} in Theorem 3.4, Corollary 3.5, and Corollary 3.7 (or alternatively state the bounds on (\EV{|c_k - \tilde{c}_k^{(m)}|^2})^{1/2}).
issues.overall_effect: The stated coefficient error bounds in Theorem 3.4 and Corollaries 3.5 and 3.7 are incorrect in their scaling with respect to the eigenvalues \lambda_k, \mu_k, and the logarithmic factor \delta_{\gamma, h}.
issues.title: Mean square error bounds in Theorem 3.4 retain un-squared factors from RMS estimates
issues.why_classification: Squaring the RHS factors directly aligns the theorem statement with its valid proof and restores consistency with the noise scaling without changing the convergence rates in h or altering any proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \leq C_{\Pi}^2 \sum_{\ell = 1}^n \left[ g_\ell^2 (t_\ell - t_{\ell - 1}) + 2 \alpha g_\ell \int_{t_{\ell - 1}}^{t_\ell} f_{t_n}(s) \, \text{d}s + \alpha^2 \int_{t_{\ell - 1}}^{t_\ell} f_{t_n}(s)^2 \, \text{d}s  \right]

issues.failure_explanation: The proof of Lemma 5.3 expands \norm{\Pi_0(g + \alpha f_{t_n})}_{L^2}^2 and attempts to bound it by comparing terms individually with the expansion of \norm{g + \alpha f_{t_n}}_{L^2}^2. This argument is mathematically invalid for several reasons: (1) the coefficient 2\alpha g_\ell can be negative, which reverses inequalities; (2) bounding each of (t_n - \tilde{s}_\ell)^{\gamma-1}(t_n - t_{\ell-1}) and (t_n - \tilde{s}_\ell)^{\gamma-1}(t_n - t_\ell) by \lesssim multiples does not bound their difference, as the difference cancels to leading order O(h_\ell); and (3) bounding individual terms in an expanded square where cross terms are indefinite does not bound the sum.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma 5.3 lacks a valid proof, leaving the hypothesis verification for the order-0 method in Corollary 3.7 unsupported.
issues.title: Invalid reasoning in proof of uniform L^2 boundedness of piecewise constant projection
issues.why_classification: Resolving this requires constructing a new nontrivial argument relying on properties of orthogonal projections rather than routine algebra, but it remains localized to Lemma 5.3 and preserves the claimed statement and all downstream results.
